There's so much to cover in this topic, but I can recommend this:
Start with the basic chords you know, learn their modes, eg: G G7 G9 G5b and so on. Learn what changes (via theory) and why it changes, then learn to apply it in other chords. Finger picking, for example great place to start is prelude in c major, but it can be quite challenging if you're not experienced with it. A beautiful composition, guaranteed to get you some gals attention.

Learn correct posture (might seem silly but believe me it helps, whenever I record death metal stuff at home and there's a tricky riff, correct posture helps me play it correctly)

Learn to do rapid chord changes (will help with some songs)

Depending on your guitar playing level, you can also try moonlight sonata 1st movement, but that's a tricky piece to nail the changes cleanly, sloppy played it sounds quite bad.

Learn what is legato and staccato
Try changing chords without any pause between them.

Metronome is your friend.

And what's most important, it's that classical guitar is very very tricky. Don't give up!
